python -c "
from more_itertools import partial_product

# Test with ones, tens, hundreds
ones = [1, 2, 3]
tens = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
hundreds = [100, 200]

result = list(partial_product(ones, tens, hundreds))
print('Result:', result)

expected = [
    (1, 10, 100),
    (2, 10, 100),
    (3, 10, 100),
    (3, 20, 100),
    (3, 30, 100),
    (3, 40, 100),
    (3, 50, 100),
    (3, 50, 200),
]
print('Expected:', expected)
print('Match:', result == expected)
" 2>&1

The real issue is that the algorithm needs to advance positions sequentially: exhaust position 0, advance it; exhaust position 1, advance it; exhaust position 2, advance it. Each advancement pulls from the next iterable in sequence, not repeatedly from the same one.

So after exhausting 'AB', we'd get 'B' as the new current value, then move to 'C', exhaust it, get 'D', move to 'DEF', and so on. The fix requires detecting when an iterable is exhausted and handling that transition properly—either by skipping the exhausted iterable or by adjusting how we track which values have already been yielded.
